summary: A bitter herb displays red-purple veins on paired green leaves. Nutrient-rich patches teach the valley's defended-leaf warning through visible foliage, grazing avoidance and specialist feeding.

chains.trait: Persistent red veins and alkaloid-bearing glandular leaves
links: Seeded biochemistry associates warning pigment with defended foliage
Alkaloids occur throughout leaves, concentrated near veins and glands
Most grazers avoid patches while specialists tolerate limited feeding
chains.play: Learn avoidance before ingestion; observe babosa and merodeador without copying their tolerance.
chains.weakness: Specialist herbivores still consume defended tissue.

plausibility.summary: Pigment–toxin association follows canon; no shared precursor is claimed. Green leaf portions remain poisonous.

analogues.mechanism: Anthocyanin overlays remain visible over green photosynthetic tissue; honest alkaloid signalling is planet-specific.

chains.trait: Enrichment-loving patches and hooked dry propagules
links: Decomposing compatible tissues enrich disturbed soil
Available nutrients support rapid growth and nitrogen-containing defence
Hooked propagules hitchhike on passing bodies
chains.play: Read irregular grazing halos and inspect attached seed capsules.
chains.weakness: Dense grass, deep shade and waterlogging suppress recruitment.

plausibility.summary: Nutrient enrichment explains placement without implying metal contamination or certain predator presence.

analogues.mechanism: Hooked fruiting structures attach to animals for external dispersal; enrichment preference is a separate fictional trait.

poison.signal: Conspicuous red-purple veins on every living leaf, including young foliage.

gameplay.notes: Ingestion causes dose-dependent nausea and impaired movement. Known clean kaolin offers partial detoxification in play, not an instant universal cure. Teach this route before optional poisoning; specialist self-medication is observational.

relations.note: Avoids feeding and leaves irregular tall-grass fringes.
Avoids toxic leaves and lacks normal detox capacity.
Tolerates foliage and incorporates defensive compounds into mucus.
Occasionally takes small amounts during self-medication.
Crust persists on adjacent exposed rock.
Later comparison teaches that alpine purple pigmentation can screen UV.

overlay_rules: Five to seven prominent red-purple secondary veins.
Preserve vein visibility across ages and lighting variants.

placement.density: Irregular enriched patches; first teaching patch in low-threat ground

generator.seasonal: Vigorous wet-season growth; approximately 5 mm hooked capsules mature as soil dries.
generator.wind_response: Stems flex; grazing halos follow local avoidance rather than fixed circles.

journal.en: Red veins, grass left tall. The slug eats what the herd refuses.
journal.es: Venas rojas, hierba sin pacer. La babosa come lo que rechaza la manada.

changelog.what: flora addendum (start valley): 7 voices drafted and peer-reviewed, Composer referee, sol chaired

observe: Learn clean kaolin access and later compare alpine UV pigmentation (F14, F25).
secrets: Its patches reveal enrichment, not nickel, impact shards or a guaranteed ambush.
